concepts.title: Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.definition: In a right triangle the trigonometric ratios of an acute angle A compare its sides: sine A is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine A is adjacent over hypotenuse, and tangent A is opposite over adjacent - with cosecant, secant and cotangent as their reciprocals.
concepts.key_idea: Name the sides opposite and adjacent to the angle, then form the ratios.
question_patterns: find all the trigonometric ratios of angle A in the given triangle
if tan A = 3/4 find the other ratios
write sin A, cos A and tan A for the given right triangle
given the sides find the value of cos A
which ratio is opposite over adjacent
if sin A = 12/13 find tan A

solution_steps.explain: Divide the opposite side by the hypotenuse.

concepts.title: Ratios of 45, 30 and 60 Degrees
concepts.definition: Geometry fixes the ratios of the standard angles: for 45 degrees both legs are equal so tan 45 = 1; halving an equilateral triangle gives sin 30 = 1/2, cos 30 = root 3 over 2, sin 60 = root 3 over 2 and cos 60 = 1/2 - values worth memorising as a table.
concepts.key_idea: Three special angles, one table: 45 gives 1, 30 and 60 swap the root three halves.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh108.txt sections on trigonometric ratios of specific angles
question_patterns: find the value of tan 45 degrees
evaluate 2 sin 30 + cos 60 using the standard values
write the values of all ratios of 30 degrees
what is the value of sin 60 cos 30 + cos 60 sin 30
compare sin 30 and sin 60 - which is larger and why
verify that tan 60 = root 3 using the table

solution_steps.explain: List the sine, cosine and tangent values for 0, 30, 45, 60 and 90 degrees.
Replace each ratio by its table value and simplify.
Give the exact value using root three where needed.

concepts.title: Trigonometric Identities
concepts.definition: Trigonometric identities hold for every angle: sin squared A + cos squared A = 1, 1 + tan squared A = sec squared A, and 1 + cot squared A = cosecant squared A; they simplify expressions and prove other relations.
concepts.key_idea: The Pythagorean identity in trigonometric dress: squares of sine and cosine always total one.
question_patterns: prove that sin squared A + cos squared A = 1
evaluate the given expression using identities
simplify (1 + tan squared A) cos squared A
express sec A in terms of sin A using identities
verify the identity for A = 30 degrees

solution_steps.explain: The identity guarantees a total of 1.

worked_examples.question_pattern: In a right triangle the side opposite angle A is {opposite} and the hypotenuse is {hypotenuse}. Find sin A.

solution_template.explain: Sine is the ratio of these two sides.

worked_examples.question_pattern: For angle A, the opposite side measures {opposite} and the hypotenuse {hypotenuse}. Compute sin A.
For angle A with sin A = {sin_a} and cos A = {cos_a}, verify the Pythagorean identity.

solution_template.explain: Compute sin A squared and cos A squared.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Given sin A = {sin_a}, use the identity to compute cos A squared.

extracted_variables.cos_a: cosine whose square is to be verified

solution_template.explain: The identity gives cos A squared.
